CEST-detectable metabolite candidates: breast

1 of 5 candidates clear the simulated with-vs-without contrast threshold (0.5%) at some field strength, by chemical exchange (downfield, +ppm) or by the relayed NOE (upfield, −ppm). 2 fall below it; 2 are unknown because no group had a verified reference rate, so nothing could be simulated. The threshold applies to our own simulation, never to a literature MTRasym.

  • Mobile protein/peptide amide pool (APT): ✓ detectable (chemical exchange)
  • Myo-inositol: ✗ not detectable
  • Glycerophosphocholine: ✗ not detectable
  • Glutamate: ? unknown (not simulated)
  • Phosphocholine: ? unknown (not simulated)

Excluded before simulation (not stored in the tissue): [model's own exclusion] Creatine (total creatine, tCr): reported by PMID 27100284 and 42687344 as CEST-active in breast, but 'total creatine' is a pooled 1H MRS grouping of creatine + phosphocreatine without a single defined concentration; no single-molecule breast concentration confirmed, so excluded.; [model's own exclusion] Glycogen (glycoCEST): searches for breast/mammary glycogen concentration returned no hits; no evidence breast parenchyma stores glycogen at >1 mM. Treated as absent/not applicable for breast.; [model's own exclusion] Glycosaminoglycans (gagCEST): searches returned no breast GAG concentration; cartilage/disc-specific target, not a major breast stromal CEST target at >1 mM. Not supported.; [model's own exclusion] Total choline (tCho) as a single pool: it is a 1H MRS peak grouping of chemically distinct choline, PC, GPC, not a single defined molecule; only its individual components (PCho, GPC) are reported.; [model's own exclusion] Lipid CH2 / phospholipid headgroup pool: MRS spectral grouping, not a single defined exchangeable-proton molecule.; [model's own exclusion] Sex steroids / retinoic acid (PMID 28928086, 35269414): present only in nM-fM range, far below 1 mM threshold.; [model's own exclusion] Dendrogenin A (PMID 31415823): cholesterol-amine conjugate at very low concentration, below 1 mM; not a CEST target.

Mobile protein/peptide amide pool (APT) — CEST: ✓ detectable (chemical exchange)

Concentration: 22.00 mM typical (20-30 mM (backbone amide protons))

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: This is an estimate, not a direct measurement. APTW signal from breast lesions (~1.5-3.2% MTRasym) confirms the mobile amide pool is CEST-active in breast (PMID 35816177, 38038421), but no abstract gives a mM number. The 20-30 mM figure is derived from typical soft-tissue protein content (~15-20% wet weight) converted to backbone amide units, assuming mobile fraction ~80-90%. No source-specific breast-tissue protein assay number was found, so the protein-fraction figure is an assumption.

Derivation stepValueSource
APT W signal is measurable and higher in malignant vs benign breast lesions, confirming mobile amide pool CEST activity in breast.APT ~1.55% (malignant) vs 0.54% (benign) MTRasymjournal_article: PMID 35816177

Convert protein mass to backbone amide units (peptide bond ~111 Da per residue).~1.36 mmol amide/g tissue (at 15% protein)calculation: 0.15 g/g / 0.111 g/mol = 1.35 mmol/g
Account for mobile fraction and tissue water density to convert g/tissue to aqueous mM.~20-30 mM in tissue watercalculation: mobile fraction ~0.8-0.9; tissue aqueous volume ~0.6-0.7 mL/g

Exchangeable protons: backbone amide NH (one per residue) (1H, +3.50 ppm, slow-to-intermediate; H-bond retarded, distinct ~3.5 ppm CEST/Z peak exchange, exchangeable); side-chain amine / epsilon-NH (Lys, free NH3+) (1H, +2.80 ppm, fast/intermediate; amine exchange broadens the peak exchange, exchangeable); non-exchangeable mobile C-H (protein backbone/side chain, rNOE) (3H, -1.00 ppm, rNOE (dipolar, relayed); non-exchangeable C-H relay saturation to water exchange, not exchangeable)

Reference database (biofluid — for comparison, not a tissue value): TISSUE — no curated breast concentration found in BioNumbers for this metabolite; the tissue number in this report is therefore not reference-grounded

Recommended field strength(s): 1.5 T, 3 T, 5 T, 7 T

Robustness to input uncertainty: fragile

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (backbone amide NH (one per residue) [amide]: concentration 20-30 mM, kex 15-158 s−1) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.10-0.22%, 1.5 T: 0.16-0.83%, 3 T: 0.22-1.13%, 5 T: 0.25-1.29%, 7 T: 0.23-1.78%. Threshold 0.5%. Only the point estimate clears the threshold; the low corner does not.

Frequency-collision analysis:

  • 0.5 T: APT (3.50 ppm) blurs with Myo-inositol OH (0.72 ppm, 59 Hz < 138 Hz linewidth) and GPC OH (1.0 ppm, 53 Hz). rNOE (-3.50 ppm) at 125.6 Hz separation vs 128 Hz linewidth - marginal blur. 1.5 T: hydroxyl collisions clear.
  • 3-7 T: only semisolid MT pool (-2.4 ppm, ~16 kHz linewidth) overlaps, but this is background, not a metabolite. Internal: amide 3.50 vs rNOE -3.50 ppm; separation grows 126 Hz (0.5 T) to 1758 Hz (7 T); resolved at 3 T and above. At 0.5 T the APT number is contaminated by hydroxyl background.

Direct water saturation: Swept B1 (0.25-0.75 µT) gives direct-sat bandwidth 10.6-31.9 Hz. APT offset is 178-1758 Hz from water. No direct-saturation masking at any field. rNOE offset is 178-1758 Hz upfield; same conclusion.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat:

  • Amide kex = 65.5 s−1 is median of two in vivo measurements (116 s−1 brain PMID 40228056; 15 s−1 generic PMID 23008121), both borrowed from brain/generic tissue -- no breast-specific in vivo amide kex.
  • The 15-158 s−1 spread the table carries is large; 7 T contrast (0.867%) is near the upper uncertainty corner (0.226-1.783%). rNOE kex = 5 s−1 from a single protein-solution phantom (PMID 25996515), not measured in any tissue -- weakest provenance. rNOE contrast (0.312% at 7 T) is an order-of-magnitude estimate.

Optimized saturation sequence by field strength (derived from a Bloch-McConnell B1×Tsat sweep):

  • 0.5 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.190% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 1.5 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Slow-exchange amide (kex ~65 s−1, omega_delta >> kex). CEST contrast peaks when omega_1 ~ sqrt(kex*R2*) ~ 114 rad/s ~ 0.2 µT at 3T; sweep optimum at 0.5 µT is slightly above strict peak due to grid resolution and direct-sat avoidance. Tsat=3s ~ 3*T1 (T1=1s), near saturation steady state. Peak B1 shifts up with B0 as offset in Hz grows.
    recommended sequence: 0.513% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 3 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Same physics as 1.5 T; 0.5 µT is the sweep optimum. At 3T the APT offset is 175 Hz from water, well outside the 21.3 Hz direct-sat bandwidth. Tsat=3s gives ~3*T1 saturation. Multi-pool Lorentzian fitting (AREX/MTRREX) required for extraction (PMID 41553443).
    recommended sequence: 0.699% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 5 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — 0.5 µT optimum. Offset 292 Hz from water at 5T; direct-sat bandwidth 21.3 Hz, no masking. Slow-exchange peak B1 unchanged from 3T. Tsat=3s.
    recommended sequence: 0.796% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 7 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Sweep optimum rises to 0.75 µT at 7T as the offset in Hz (385 Hz) grows and the optimal omega_1*T_sat product must hold. Direct-sat bandwidth 31.9 Hz, still far from APT offset. Best contrast in the set (0.867%). Multi-pool Lorentzian (AREX/MTRREX) essential; MTRasym inadequate (PMID 41553443).
    recommended sequence: 0.867% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied

B1/Tsat vs. extraction method (click for note + literature)

Note: MTRasym is inadequate for APT in breast (PMID 41553443: no subtype separation with MTRasym; AREX and MTRREX worked at 9.4 T with 5-pool Lorentzian). Recommended: AREX or MTRREX from multi-pool Lorentzian fitting with dense Z-spectrum (>=40 offsets, +/-5 ppm) and >=2 B1 powers. MTRasym acceptable only as screening; inherits fat artifacts (PMID 31532006) and rNOE/MT contamination.

Potential clinical impact

amide (APT, 3.5 ppm): 7 CEST/NOE application and 0 metabolite-change studies verified (6 human, 1 animal; 516 humans, 0 animals; 2 dropped by verification). APT (3.5 ppm) CEST is the best-established breast pool. Applied in humans for differential diagnosis of early-stage/benign vs malignant breast lesions (MTRasym lower in malignancy), for TNBC molecular-subtype prediction (APTw higher in TNBC than HER2+), and for predicting pathological response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (APTw higher in responders; signal falls during therapy). Also used in breast-cancer-related lymphedema (PTR'APT rises post-therapy), in menstrual-cycle fibroglandular tissue at 7 T, and in mouse breast models (divergent trends). No non-CEST direct measurement of the mobile amide pool in breast was found.

Caveats / critique (6 points, 322 words) — 22 mM mobile amide NH concentration is consistent with APT literature (PMID 31136039) showing APT correlates with mobile protein concentration in breast. 15-30 …
  • 22 mM mobile amide NH concentration is consistent with APT literature (PMID 31136039) showing APT correlates with mobile protein concentration in breast. 15-30 mM range reasonable. Compartment issue: simulation does not model intracellular vs extracellular fraction. Fat content in breast (~50-70%) is a known APT-CEST confounder (PMID 31532006) not in the simulation. Backbone amide class correct.
  • Side-chain amine class correct but not simulated (no reference). rNOE group: chemist wrote -1.0 ppm but simulation used -3.5 ppm; the -3.5 matches literature (PMID 36929814, 28272761, 36965064). Chemist's -1.0 is wrong; simulation's -3.5 is correct. rNOE n_protons=3 is a rough class-level estimate, not molecule-specific. Pool T1=1.0 s, T2=10 ms are generic small-solute values, not measured for this protein pool.
  • In vivo APT-CEST literature (PMID 37641066) uses 3.2-3.6 ppm range for APT in murine breast; simulation used 3.5 ppm. Consistent. rNOE at -3.5 ppm matches in vivo measurements (PMID 36965064 at 3 T, 28272761 at 9.4 T). Side-chain amines (Lys epsilon-NH2, Arg guanidinium) are real but were classed as 'amine' and not simulated due to missing reference.
  • Arg guanidinium (if present) would be a distinct class (guanidinium) at ~2 ppm, not captured. No OH on backbone. The pool is treated as a single amide group; in reality it is a distribution of amide environments with slightly different shifts.
  • Groups not simulated: side-chain amine / epsilon-NH (Lys, free NH3+) [amine] -- the reference table has no verified exchange rate and shift for amine protons -- we don't know; not simulated no SAR or hardware ceiling is applied: the recommended B1/Tsat is the sweep optimum, and deliverability must be checked against the scanner's SAR monitor
  • Primary established CEST target in breast. APT imaging is a well-validated breast contrast (PMID 35816177, 38038421). Concentration must be estimated; no abstract gave a protein or amide mM number. [Unsourced reasoning] 1 numeric step(s) rest on an unsourced assumption: 'Typical soft-tissue protein content ~15-20% of wet weight.'.

Robustness to input uncertainty: upper-bound only

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (ring hydroxyl OH x6 [hydroxyl]: concentration 1-5 mM, kex fixed at 600 s−1 (single measurement, spread unknown)) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.01-0.05%, 1.5 T: 0.02-0.09%, 3 T: 0.04-0.22%, 5 T: 0.09-0.43%, 7 T: 0.13-0.65%. Threshold 0.5%. The point estimate is below threshold; only the high corner clears it.

Frequency-collision analysis: 0.5 T: at 0.72 ppm, 59 Hz from APT (blurs), 5.9 Hz from GPC OH (completely merged). 1.5 T: APT clears; GPC 17.6 Hz vs 223 Hz linewidth, still merged. 3-7 T: GPC separation grows 35-82 Hz, still < 223 Hz linewidth -- never resolves from GPC OH at any field. Myo-inositol and GPC are spectrally indistinguishable as hydroxyl CEST peaks in this candidate set. Semisolid MT overlap is background, not a metabolite.

Direct water saturation: 0.72 ppm offset = 24-297 Hz from water across fields. Swept B1 (0.1-1.0 µT) gives direct-sat bandwidth 4.3-42.6 Hz. At 0.5 T and 1.5 T the small offset means direct water saturation is a real confound; the exchange contrast is partly masked by the direct-saturation tail.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: kex = 600 s−1 from human brain in vivo at 7T (PMID 20951217), N=5. NOT from breast, NOT from phantom. Provenance flags 'borrowed from brain, human, human in vivo'. Brain vs breast pH, temperature, macromolecular crowding can shift OH kex by factor 2-3. Single measurement, no range, no uncertainty corners for kex. Contrast values are order-of-magnitude.

B1/Tsat vs. extraction method (click for note + literature)

Note: Fast-exchange, low-offset OH pool: MTRasym unreliable (direct-sat dominated). AREX or multi-pool Lorentzian fit needed in principle. But the practical blocker is the hydroxyl band shared with GPC -- no single-offset metric isolates myo-inositol. The 2016 study (PMID 27100284) used a full multi-offset metabolic CEST profile, the only sensible extraction route, requiring a metabolite-specific reference profile.

Potential clinical impact

myo-inositol (OH CEST): 0 CEST/NOE application and 2 metabolite-change studies verified (2 human, 0 animal; 110 humans, 0 animals; 1 dropped by verification). No CEST/NOE application of myo-inositol in breast was found. Metabolite-change evidence is ex vivo: in 1.5 T in vivo breast MRS the 3.2 ppm composite (containing myo-inositol) was not a unique malignancy marker; in HR-MAS breast-cancer metabolomics myo-inositol correlated with transcripts and was elevated specifically in Luminal B (HER2+) tumors. The simulation found myo-inositol not detectable at any listed field for breast, consistent with the lack of imaging evidence.

Robustness to input uncertainty: no

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (aliphatic/primary hydroxyl OH x2 (C1, C2) [hydroxyl]: concentration 0.5-2 mM, kex fixed at 600 s−1 (single measurement, spread unknown)) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.00-0.01%, 1.5 T: 0.01-0.02%, 3 T: 0.01-0.04%, 5 T: 0.02-0.08%, 7 T: 0.03-0.12%. Threshold 0.5%.

Frequency-collision analysis: 0.5 T: at 1.00 ppm, 53 Hz from APT (blurs), 5.9 Hz from myo-inositol OH (0.72 ppm) -- completely merged. 1.5 T: 17.6 Hz from myo-inositol, linewidth 223 Hz -- still fully merged. 3-7 T: 35-82 Hz from myo-inositol, still < 223 Hz linewidth -- never resolves from myo-inositol OH at any field. GPC and myo-inositol are spectrally indistinguishable in this candidate set as hydroxyl CEST peaks. APT collision clears at 1.5 T. Semisolid MT is background.

Direct water saturation: 1.00 ppm offset = 70-460 Hz from water. Swept B1 (0.25-1.0 µT) gives direct-sat bandwidth 10.6-42.6 Hz. At 0.5 T and 1.5 T the small offset means direct water saturation is a real confound. At 3-7 T the offset is large enough that direct-sat is less of an issue, but the contrast is still far below threshold.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: kex = 600 s−1 is BORROWED FROM MYO-INOSITOL'S BRAIN IN VIVO MEASUREMENT (PMID 20951217). This is the weakest provenance: (a) different metabolite, (b) different tissue (brain, not breast), (c) single value with no range. A primary alcohol OH on GPC may exchange at a different rate than a myo-inositol ring OH (steric, pKa, H-bonding differences), potentially by factor 2-5. Simulated contrast (0.057% at 7T) is an order-of-magnitude estimate, direction of bias unknown.

Note: If ever detectable, fast OH exchange + collision with myo-inositol means only a full multi-offset metabolic CEST profile (as in PMID 27100284) could apportion the hydroxyl band among GPC, myo-inositol, and other OH metabolites. No single-ppm metric works. In practice, the contrast (0.057% at 7T, upper corner 0.115%) is an order of magnitude below the 0.5% detectability bar, so no extraction method is practical.

Note:

  • If a kex were available, the fast-exchange amine regime (likely kex >> 100 s−1) would call for AREX or MTRasym at moderate B1. But the practical blocker is the amine band (1.8-3 ppm) shared by glutamine, phosphocholine, GPC, and free amines.
  • GluCEST (PMID 30072394) uses a saturation offset near the glutamate-specific amine position and relies on glutaminase-inhibition response for specificity -- functional validation rather than spectral isolation. Without a glutamate-specific kex, no extraction method separates it from the amine background in breast.

glutamate (GluCEST, ~2.0 ppm): 1 CEST/NOE application and 3 metabolite-change studies verified (3 human, 1 animal; 199 humans, 17 animals; 0 dropped by verification). Caveats / critique (6 points, 295 words) — 1 mM is a reasonable order for phosphocholine in breast tumor MRS (typically 0.5-5 mM in the choline-containing compounds resonance). Concentration is fine. The…
  • 1 mM is a reasonable order for phosphocholine in breast tumor MRS (typically 0.5-5 mM in the choline-containing compounds resonance). Concentration is fine. The issue is purely chemical: phosphocholine has no exchangeable proton at pH 7.4. CRITICAL STRUCTURAL ERROR. Agent 2 identifies a 'secondary amine NH (choline backbone)' -- this proton does not exist. Phosphocholine is PhO3(2-)-O-CH2-CH2-N+(CH3)3.
  • The nitrogen is QUATERNARY ammonium (N+ with four C bonds, no H). There is no exchangeable amine proton. The only potential exchangeable group is the phosphate P-OH, but at pH 7.4 (pKa ~1-2) it is fully deprotonated -- no pool. The two O-CH2 groups are non-exchangeable C-H. Phosphocholine has effectively NO CEST pool at physiological pH.
  • The NOT SIMULATED flag is right in outcome (no contrast) but the chemist's reasoning (a 'secondary amine NH') is a structural error that should be corrected. N/A -- no CEST peak to place. No in vivo phosphocholine CEST study found in searches (3 targeted queries, 0 results). None exist.
  • The 'secondary amine NH' Agent 2 listed is not in the molecule. At pH 7.4, phosphocholine has zero exchangeable protons. Not simulated: secondary amine NH (choline backbone) [amine] -- the reference table has no verified exchange rate and shift for amine protons -- we don't know; not simulated
  • Chemist agent's proposed structure was WRONG and has been replaced with PubChem's verified structure for 'Phosphocholine'. Rejected SMILES: '[O-]P(=O)(O)OC[C@H](N)CC[N+](C)(C)C'; PubChem: 'C[N+](C)(C)CCOP(=O)(O)O'. The exchangeable-proton groups below are still the chemist's own analysis and may have been reasoned from the wrong structure. Choline CEST at ~3.1 ppm. Absolute-quantification studies exist (PMID 24036926) but numeric values are in tables, not abstracts. Verify full-text.
  • [Unsourced reasoning] 1 numeric step(s) rest on an unsourced assumption: 'Assign ~1 mM order-of-magnitude estimate for a membrane-biosynthesis i'.

In vivo verification: ROI-differential CEST scan — Coronal slab through the breast, centred at the nipple-areolar level on a 3T body array. Slab spans the entire breast from skin to chest wall and extends to include the ipsilateral liver dome, a paraspinal muscle stripe, and chest wall.

Why this scan:

  • A single Z-spectrum acquisition sweeps all candidate pools at once, but the real discriminator is ROI-contrast that tracks known amide-protein differences. Fibroglandular tissue is protein-dense and gives strong 3.5 ppm APT; fat gives near-zero mobile amide (and a strong upfield lipid-NOE).
  • Comparing the two in the same slab at matched B0/B1 separates genuine amide-exchange contrast from generic MT/NOE, which would not fall the same way. Adding liver and paraspinal muscle (both in the pipeline tissue table) gives a second independent protein-concentration axis.
  • If the 3.5 ppm peak tracks protein content while the -1 to -1.7 ppm NOE peak tracks lipid fraction, the effect is metabolite-specific.
ROIWhere it is drawnRole
breast fibroglandular tissue target tissueLargest region of dense glandular/fibrous parenchyma between the nipple and chest wall, on the high-signal fibroglandular core of the Coronal slab. ~2-4 cm diameter.TARGET. Protein-dense mobile amide pool; expected strongest 3.5 ppm APT peak. Primary verification ROI.
breast adipose tissue target tissueHypointense subcutaneous fat layer between skin and parenchyma in the same coronal slab, excluding any fibroglandular contamination.TARGET (composition contrast). Near-zero mobile amide but strong upfield lipid-NOE; provides the low-protein / high-lipid end of the differential.
liverHepatic parenchyma in the upper abdomen within the lower part of the slab, ~2-3 cm from the dome, away from vessels and the gallbladder.COMPARISON. High protein/water content, low fat, in the pipeline tissue table; independent reference for 3.5 ppm APT in a non-breast tissue.
paraspinal muscleErector spinae / paraspinal muscle stripe posterior to the thoracic vertebrae, in the posterior part of the slab.COMPARISON. Intermediate protein, low fat, in the pipeline table; mid-concentration reference. Used as a B1/MT sanity check.
subcutaneous fatDeep fat band of the chest wall / anterior trunk posterior to the breast and lateral to the liver, in the posterior-inferior part of the slab.COMPARISON / fat reference. Pure low-protein, high-lipid tissue; validates the lipid-NOE signature and the low-amide floor.

Scan protocol: 3 T, pulsed rectangular (sinc) train, duty-cycled, B1=0.75 µT, 100 pulses × 15 ms (interpulse delay 15 ms, duty cycle 50%), total Tsat=3000 ms, TR=3200 ms

SAR reasoning (the experimentalist agent's own; the pipeline applies no SAR model):

  • Mean B1 0.75 µT with 50% duty cycle over ~3 s gives time-averaged SAR well under the 3T whole-body limit (~0.6-0.8 W/kg) for a superficial breast/chest-wall slab. SAR scales as B1^2 x duty cycle x Tsat; here B1 is at the upper end of the low-B1 CEST range and duty is 0.5, keeping the product modest.
  • Breast is superficial so the body-coil E-field deposition here is not the worst-case deep-organ region; still, use the smallest FOV/shortest readout that covers the slab and verify head/body coil loading in a pre-scan SAR check.

Compromise rationale:

  • The physicist agent gave the amide pool its strongest 3T case at B1~0.5-0.75 µT / ~3-4 s, and the same single candidate (amides + amine + NOE) covers all targeted pools. I set B1 = 0.75 µT, Tsat ~3 s, 50% duty.
  • This slightly favors the slow-exchange amide (3.5 ppm) which wants longer saturation at moderate B1, and adequately saturates the faster amine (2.8 ppm). The rNOE (relayed, non-exchangeable) is less sensitive to Tsat and is well-served at this B1.
  • One protocol cannot be simultaneously optimal for every pool, so the B1 sweep at 0.7x/1.3x will show how much of the prediction survives B1 inhomogeneity.

Fat suppression:

  • 3D CEST-Dixon (3-point, e.g. SPIR-like water-selective excitation with fat/water separation). Rationale: the breast is intrinsically a fat/parenchyma mixture; fat's own upfield lipid spectrum and its MT/NOE overlap the rNOE region and would otherwise masquerade as a metabolite effect.
  • Water-selective excitation plus Dixon water/fat separation lets me (a) exclude fat signal from the parenchymal MTRasym and (b) deliberately KEEP the fat image to use it as the low-protein/high-lipid comparison ROI. Without separation the fat peak would contaminate the 3.5 ppm APT measurement.

Motion mitigation:

  • Breath-hold is impractical for a ~3 s saturation + Z-spectrum sweep across many offsets, so use respiratory navigator-gated or respiratory-triggered acquisition with cardiac awareness (slab reaches the liver dome/chest wall). The breast is relatively motion-stable but diaphragmatic motion shifts the liver ROI.
  • Use a respiratory bellows trigger to gate acquisition during end-expiration, and re-slice to re-centre the liver ROI each breath if gating is tight. This extends scan time to ~10-20 min, acceptable for a research verification protocol. Patient breathes normally; no sedation needed.

Slice coverage: Coronal slab, ~3-5 cm thick (1-3 overlapping 3D partitions or a single 6-8 mm slab with a 3D turbo-readout), centred at the nipple-areolar level, FOV ~28-32 cm AP x 20-24 cm LR to span from skin of the breast to the chest wall and inferiorly into the upper abdomen to include the liver dome, and posteriorly to capture a paraspinal muscle stripe and chest-wall subcutaneous fat. Resolution ~2.5-3 mm in-plane, 6-8 mm through-slab.

Structures in FOV: breast fibroglandular tissue, breast adipose tissue, liver, paraspinal muscle, subcutaneous fat, chest wall, pectoral muscle, thoracic vertebral body (posterior margin)

Z-spectrum sampling offsets:

  • -8.00 ppm: far-off baseline reference (no pool)
  • -5.00 ppm: baseline / MT tail reference
  • -4.00 ppm: rNOE / lipid-NOE region (upfield)
  • -3.50 ppm: symmetric reference for amide MTRasym
  • -3.00 ppm: rNOE / lipid-NOE region (upfield)
  • -2.80 ppm: symmetric reference for amine MTRasym
  • -2.50 ppm: symmetric reference for amine MTRasym
  • -2.00 ppm: lipid-NOE peak region
  • -1.70 ppm: rNOE / lipid-NOE own offset (mirror)
  • -1.50 ppm: rNOE / lipid-NOE (mobile aliphatic C-H)
  • -1.00 ppm: rNOE / lipid-NOE (mobile aliphatic C-H)
  • -0.80 ppm: rNOE / lipid-NOE symmetric reference (mirror)
  • -0.50 ppm: NOE tail / B0 reference
  • +0.00 ppm: water (0 ppm)
  • +0.50 ppm: hydroxyl/glycogen tail, MTRasym baseline
  • +1.00 ppm: amine/glycogen region, MTRasym baseline
  • +2.00 ppm: amine tail, MTRasym baseline
  • +2.50 ppm: amine CEST (side-chain NH2)
  • +2.80 ppm: amine CEST (Lys/epsilon-NH, free NH3+)
  • +3.00 ppm: amine CEST tail
  • +3.50 ppm: amide CEST (APT, backbone NH)
  • +4.00 ppm: amide tail, MTRasym baseline
  • +5.00 ppm: far baseline
  • +6.00 ppm: far-off baseline reference (no pool)
  • +8.00 ppm: far-off baseline reference (no pool)

Differential analysis plan:

  • For each ROI, average the Z-spectrum over the ROI and compute MTRasym(omega) = [S(-omega)-S(+omega)] / 2*S(0) after B0 (WASSR or 0-ppm) and B1 (magnitude-ratio) correction, plus a T1-normalised MTRasym. At the amide offset (3.5 ppm and its -3.5 mirror) plot MTRasym for all five ROIs.
  • Confirmation of a genuine amide effect: the 3.5 ppm MTRasym ranks fibroglandular > liver > paraspinal muscle >> adipose >~ subcutaneous fat, tracking the protein-concentration ordering, while the upfield -1 to -2 ppm rNOE/lipid peak ranks the reverse (fat/parenchymal-fat highest).
  • If instead all ROIs show a similar 3.5 ppm value irrespective of protein content, the effect is generic MT/NOE, not metabolite-specific. Use a Wilcoxon/Mann-Whitney across ROIs at each offset.
  • A metabolite-specific APT contribution is confirmed when (a) the 3.5 ppm peak scales with the protein axis and (b) the upfield NOE peak scales with the lipid axis, i.e. the two pools anti-correlate across ROIs. If the contrast collapses to a single value across ROIs or does not follow the concentration ordering, the result is inconclusive for that metabolite.

Not actively targeted: Myo-inositol, glycerophosphocholine, glutamate, and phosphocholine were not actively targeted. They are low/absent in the physicist agent's simulated with-vs-without contrast at 3T and fall outside this single-scan budget. They also exchange at offsets (glycerophosphocholine ~0.5-2 ppm, myo-inositol OH ~0-2 ppm, glutamate ~2 ppm, phosphocholine choline-methyl ~3 ppm) that overlap the amide/amine region here, so a dedicated low-B1 multi-pool fit or separate protocol would be needed; not designed in this plan.

Caveats:

  • Real limits: (1) ROI partial volume -- the fibroglandular core is interdigitated with fat, so even careful ROI placement mixes amide and lipid signal; use the Dixon water-only image to minimise. (2) B0/B1 inhomogeneity across the slab (breast to liver to chest wall) can differ even after WASSR/magnitude-ratio correction; the 0.7x/1.3x B1 re-simulation shows how much of the prediction survives.
  • (3) Susceptibility at the chest-wall/bone boundary can distort the Z-spectrum near the posterior ROIs. (4) One compromise B1/Tsat cannot be simultaneously optimal for every pool; the amine and amide may not both be at peak sensitivity.
  • (5) Concentrations for the comparison ROIs are reasoned estimates (no direct tissue-specific APT-concentration papers found); they set the expected direction of the differential but not exact magnitudes, so the test is a contrast-ordering (sign/direction) argument rather than an absolute quantification. (6) Respiratory gating shifts the liver ROI across breaths; the differential relies on consistent re-slicing.
